verdict.rationale: Groq's first-party docs describe remote MCP support in the Responses API. A user supplies an MCP server URL plus authentication, and Groq handles all tool orchestration, so the model uses that server's tools with no tool logic written by the user. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP tool use, and evidence of support beyond remote HTTPS servers (e.g. local/stdio servers) along with deeper detail on auth and tool-filtering options.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Groq supports remote tool use via MCP servers, allowing you to simply point to an MCP server URL and the Groq API will start using its tools without you having to implement any tool logic yourself.
Groq's Responses API supports remote tool use via MCP servers via HTTPS where Groq handles all orchestration... You don't implement anything - just provide the MCP server URL and authentication.
